answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each node to stake a token that depreciates over time, much like copper left exposed to damp. If a fake account goes idle, its stake corrodes and the balance drops below the entry threshold, so it gets pruned like weeds pulled from a neglected garden. A real user who keeps working maintains their stake against erosion, and the network can still verify activity even when legitimate nodes sit underground like karst.
